title: Go-To-Market Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Growth at Private Equity Insights

Are you excited about solving real, hard problems? Are you looking to work in an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people? And do you want real ownership from your first week? If so, now is the time to apply for the Growth role at Private Equity Insights.

The mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.

You will work in sprints and get fast execution under your skin. You will learn to write copy that makes elite investors act, map the entire market of investors, decide who to target, and deploy AI to outperform a teams of 20+ people.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career, apply.

Why Private Equity Insights

Private Equity Insights is the world’s largest Private Equity community with 1m PE professionals, delivering impact through 12 global PE conferences with thousands of the world’s best investors and operators such as Blackstone, BlackRock, Apollo, Carlyle, CVC, KKR, and many more.

Private Equity Insights is part of United Media (https://www.united-media.com/) which focuses on building large-scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, finance, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 5 media companies and exited 1.

What we offer you

  • Ownership from the very start. You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way
  • Unlimited growth potential. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.
  • Skills that compound for life. Fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.
  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.
  • Travel opportunity. You will be joining our conferences

Your Responsibilities

Your responsibilities will vary; however, some of them will be to:

  • Build the audience. Identify, target, and convert every fund into our community, and make sure each one receives the right message, at the right time, and never one too many.
  • Own marketing channels that drive revenue. Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue
  • Write copy that persuades. Every email, landing page and post. Become the best copywriter and leverage it at scale with AI.
  • Sprint, test, implement. Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.
  • Build systems, not one-offs. Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.
  • Do whatever it takes to win. Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value to the client.

What we expect from you

You possess an unparalleled work ethic with a high sense of urgency. You have a relentless drive and desire to be the very best at what you do. You take ownership of everything you do, are proactive and follow through on commitments. Moreover, you’re humble and you share our passion for building and executing new businesses. Furthermore, we expect that you:

  • 1 to 3 years of experience
  • Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results
  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.
  • Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency
  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do
  • Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do
  • A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people
  • Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise

Practical details

Role is full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week.

Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year.

The start date is flexible.

Deshalb setzen wir auf ein hybrides Arbeitskonzept, das dir die Freiheit gibt, immer genau so zu arbeiten, wie es am besten zu deinen Aufgaben passt. Du brauchst neue Impulse auf internationalem Niveau? Mit Workflex bieten wir, abhängig von deiner Verantwortung, die Möglichkeit, deine Tätigkeit bis zu 30 Tage im Jahr ins Ausland zu verlegen.

  • Grown-up Business & Startup Spirit - In unserem modernen Office in Berlin-Friedrichshain findest du von höhenverstellbaren Tischen, Tischtennisplatte bis gefüllten Getränkekühlschränken und Barista-Coffee alles was das Herz begehrt.

  • Dein Kick-start bei Enpal - Onboarding-Tag mit Welcome Bag, Buddy-Programm und einem Team, das dich wirklich abholt.

  • Bleib auf dem Laufenden & gestalte mit -Transparente All-Hands, kurze Entscheidungswege und eine offene Feedback-Kultur, denn ohne Fehler gibt es keinen Fortschritt.

  • Energiewende geht nur gemeinsam - Bei Enpal erwartet dich ein legendärer Teamspirit und unvergessliche Team- und Companyevents.

  • Dein Extra-Boost -29 Urlaubstage + je ein freier Tag an Heilig Abend & Silvester, vergünstigte Mitgliedschaft bei Wellhub und Corporate Benefits. Alles, was dir hilft, Arbeit und Leben gut zu verbinden.

  • Mache dein Zuhause smart – Nachhaltigkeit fängt in den eigenen vier Wänden an. Als Teil des Teams profitierst du von dauerhaften 25% Rabatt auf das gesamte Bosch Smart Home Sortiment – für ein noch effizienteres und vernetzteres Zuhause.

 

Wir bei Enpal sind stolz auf die Vielfältigkeit unseres Teams. Weder bei der Einstellung noch während des Beschäftigungsverhältnisses werden Entscheidungen auf Basis von Hautfarbe, Religion oder religiösen Glaubens, ethnischer oder nationaler Herkunft, Nationalität, Geschlechteridentität, sexuelle Orientierung, Behinderung oder Alter getroffen. descriptionHtml:
Mit Geschmack, Gespür und Grafikverstand.

Design liegen Dir im Blut. Oder Du bist auf dem besten Weg zum Coder? Erste Seiten sind bereits online? Lass sehen, wir sind gespannt!

Aufgaben

Deine Aufgaben?

Mach die Dinge hübsch. Mit Verstand. Und mit Power.

Von der Website über Logos bis zum Magazin – und zwischendurch noch ein paar knackige Slides und clevere Social-Media-Post. Du unterstützt und entwickelst: Konzept, Ideen, Text. Du filmst, fotografierst, machst Bildbearbeitung. Und du wendest an: als planen, posten, schalten, auswerten, berichten.
Das volle Programm, ohne Rücksicht auf Vorlieben: mal verspielt, mal streng, mal laut, mal leise. Hauptsache gut.

KI? Nutzt Du mit – nicht blind, aber clever. Für schnellere Ideen, bessere Moodboards oder das erste Wording zum Visual.

Wir sehen KI als Werkzeug. Den kreativen Kopf dahinter ersetzt sie nicht – und genau der bist Du. Deswegen schick uns keine Bewerbung, die die KI für dich geschrieben hat, sondern eine ganz persönliche.

Qualifikation

Was Du mitbringen solltest?

Bring mit, was Du kannst: Ausbildung, Studium, Quereinstieg – alles gut. Hauptsache Talent. Ohne das wird’s schwierig.

Du brauchst kein abgeschlossenes Designstudium, aber ein gutes Auge, Lust auf Gestaltung und den Anspruch, Dinge besser zu machen.

Gute Laune hilft. Energie auch.

Und Deutsch? Muss sitzen. Mit Punkt, Komma und allem drum und dran. Auch, wenn Du nicht textest – wir lesen, was Du schreibst.

Benefits

Was Du bekommst?

Kaffee. Klar. Wasser und Obst auch. Und Müsli.

Dazu: spannende Kunden, echte Projekte und ein Team, das nicht nur nett tut, sondern wirklich nett ist. Arbeiten auf Augenhöhe – mit Hirn, Herz und Haltung.

Homeoffice? Klar. In der Regel 2 Tage die Woche.

Und falls Du Awards magst: Uns wurden in den letzten drei Jahren fünfzehn Preise verliehen. Nicht, weil wir’s drauf anlegen. Sondern weil wir’s ernst meinen.

Zum Schluss noch das:

Wir emotionalisieren Unternehmen.

Wir beraten, gestalten, planen – entwickeln Strategien und Konzepte, die nicht nur gut aussehen, sondern auch wirken.

Und wir begleiten unsere Kunden so lange, bis aus guten Ideen echte Ergebnisse werden.

Unsere Agentur? Mitten in Karlsruhe, in der Straße, wo sich Kunst, Kulinarik, Kultur und Kreativität treffen: die Waldstraße.

Super angebunden mit Bahn und Bus, gut erreichbar mit dem Rad, dem Scooter oder dem Auto – und einfach ein guter Ort zum Arbeiten.

Was Dich hier erwartet? Coole Kunden. Kreative Kolleg:innen auf Augenhöhe.

Und eine gesunde Mischung aus Präsenz und Homeoffice – aktuell zwei Tage die Woche remote.

Wir freuen uns auf Dich. Wirklich.

Bitte schau, dass deine Bewerbung einen CV, ein Portfolio, ein paar Zeugnisse und ein kleines Anschreiben beinhaltet.

We're hiring a Growth PM to own data and growth experimentation across the full funnel, from landing page through to in-app and pricing. ElevenLabs drives significant paid and organic traffic across self-serve, developer, and enterprise funnels; your job is to turn more of it into subscriptions, pipeline, and revenue.

You'll own the experimentation engine end to end: uncovering opportunities through funnel and product data, building and prioritizing the testing backlog, designing and evaluating experiments, and owning the tracking and reporting that turns results into decisions. Your scope runs deeper than conversion optimization: you'll drive experiments across onboarding, activation, and pricing, and align paid media, design, engineering, and product teams around one optimization roadmap.

The ideal candidate is equal parts analyst, strategist, and operator: someone who finds revenue hiding in funnel and product data, ships a high-velocity testing program, and communicates results in terms of subscriptions and pipeline, not just conversion rates.

Requirements

  • A track record of running high-velocity experimentation programs end to end - hypothesis, prioritization, test design, and analysis - with measurable revenue impact

  • Experience running experiments beyond the marketing site: in-product (onboarding, activation) and pricing or monetization

  • Deep analytics fluency: comfortable living in product analytics tools (e.g., PostHog, Amplitude, GA4) to diagnose funnel drop-off, segment traffic, and attribute outcomes across multi-domain journeys

  • Strong statistical literacy: you know how to size tests, avoid false winners, and choose the right success metric (revenue and subscriptions over clicks)

  • A cross-functional operator who can align paid media, design, engineering, and product teams around a shared optimization roadmap

Bonus

  • Experience optimizing PLG/self-serve funnels alongside sales-assisted (demo/contact-sales) funnels

Location

This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Bangalore, Dublin, London, New York, San Francisco, Tokyo, and Warsaw.

title: hbo-stage Social Media & Content Creatie
descriptionHtml:
hbo-praktijkstage, vanaf februari 2027

Ben jij creatief, nieuwsgierig en krijg je energie van social media die écht impact maakt?
Grijp de kans om jouw ideeën tot leven te brengen en zichtbaar te maken voor een groot publiek.

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Tijdens jouw stage bij het CBS duik je in de wereld van social media en ga je actief bijdragen aan het zichtbaar en begrijpelijk maken van belangrijke maatschappelijke cijfers.
Je krijgt de kans om jouw creativiteit in te zetten en verder te ontwikkelen. Je bedenkt nieuwe formats, werkt bestaande concepten uit en vertaalt complexe informatie naar content die mensen echt bereikt. Samen met het socialmediateam werk je aan sterke, herkenbare en aansprekende content.

Dit is wat je gaat doen:

  • Je ontwikkelt creatieve socialmediaformats die aansluiten bij de doelgroep en strategie van het CBS.

  • Je maakt content die daadwerkelijk wordt gepubliceerd op de socialmediakanalen van het CBS. Daarmee lever je een directe bijdrage aan de communicatie van een maatschappelijke organisatie.

  • Je vertaalt statistische informatie naar heldere en toegankelijke verhalen voor een breed publiek.

  • Je denkt actief mee over hoe het CBS zich creatief en onderscheidend kan positioneren op social media.

  • Je draagt bij aan content die impact heeft: jouw werk wordt gezien door een groot publiek en helpt mensen Nederland en de cijfers beter te begrijpen.

Dit is jouw stageplek bij CBS Den Haag

Je komt terecht in het socialmediateam van het CBS: een klein, hecht team waarin we in een informele sfeer samenwerken. De lijnen zijn kort en er is volop ruimte om ideeën te delen en initiatief te nemen.
We zijn continu op zoek naar manieren om onze content beter, creatiever en relevanter te maken. Dat betekent dat we graag experimenteren met formats, inspelen op trends en openstaan voor frisse perspectieven.

Dit breng jij mee

Je volgt een creatieve hbo-opleiding, zoals Communication & Multimedia Design, Creative Business of een vergelijkbare opleiding.

Je hebt kennis van en wellicht ervaring met:

  • Canva;

  • Adobe Creative Cloud;

  • het monteren van short-formcontent;

  • de nieuwste trends op social media.

Je denkt in mogelijkheden en krijgt energie van samenwerken.

Je hebt een ondernemende instelling en komt met innovatieve ideeën.

Dit kun je van ons verwachten

Een fijne leeromgeving waarin je:

  • jouw creatieve en socialmediaskills verder ontwikkelt in een professionele en informele werkomgeving;

  • leert om complexe statistische informatie te vertalen naar begrijpelijke en toegankelijke content voor een breed publiek;

  • effectief samenwerkt met betrokken collega's in een professioneel team.

Voor jouw inzet ontvang je een stagevergoeding van € 800,- bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur per week).

Samen met je stagebegeleider stem je af hoe je hybride kunt werken, met flexibele werktijden en de optie om deels vanuit huis aan jouw stageopdracht te werken.

Het betreft een stageopdracht en geen werkervaringsplek. Voordat je aan de stage begint verwachten we dat je vanuit de onderwijsinstelling een stagebegeleider hebt, waarmee de stage is afgestemd en concrete leerdoelen zijn afgesproken.

title: Head of Applied Research
descriptionHtml:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

Kraken is building the next generation of AI technologies for the energy sector, and we're looking for an exceptional Head of Applied Research to help lead that ambition.

As the advanced technology platform powering some of the world's largest energy utilities, Kraken has a unique combination of deep energy domain expertise along with technological rigor in AI and optimisation, offering a unique opportunity to develop AI technologies that shape how energy systems operate.

Kraken has been investing in the development of energy-specific AI models and intelligent decision-making systems to power products that can understand, predict and ultimately help shape how energy is consumed, managed and distributed.

This isn't a traditional research lab. Our focus is on building technically ambitious, commercially valuable AI systems that solve real-world problems. We want to push the boundaries of what's technically possible while ensuring that the technology we develop translates into meaningful products, measurable impact and lasting competitive advantage.

Reporting into and working closely with our Chief AI Officer, you'll help define Kraken's applied research strategy, establish the technical foundations for our next generation products and cultivate an exceptional team capable of delivering them.

This is an opportunity for someone who combines deep technical expertise with the ambition to build something genuinely new - someone who is equally comfortable with the latest literature in the field, making difficult technical decisions and turning breakthrough ideas into implementable products.

🏡 What you'll own

Shape Kraken's next generation of AI technology

  • Partner with our Chief AI Officer to define and execute Kraken's applied research strategy and roadmap, identifying the foundational capabilities and proprietary technologies that will create lasting competitive advantage.

  • Lead the development of advanced AI models and architectures designed to understand and model complex energy systems, behavior, and decision-making.

  • Explore and develop approaches using foundation models, deep learning, transformer architectures, representation learning as well as emerging techniques to unlock new capabilities.

  • Develop generalisable models capable of supporting multiple products and applications per client.

  • Establish a technical roadmap that balances ambitious innovation with practical development, scalability and commercial outcomes.

Develop and lead an exceptional technical team

  • Develop, lead a high-performing team of AI researchers, research engineers and data scientists.

  • Establish a culture of technological excellence, intellectual curiosity, experimentation and strong execution.

  • Remain close to the technology, providing hands-on technical direction, challenging data modeling and architectural decisions and helping solve complex modelling problems.

  • Attract and develop exceptional technical talent, creating an environment where highly capable individuals can do the best work of their careers.

  • Set clear technical priorities, development standards and measures of success while giving the team the autonomy to explore ambitious ideas.

Develop proprietary AI models and intelligent systems

  • Lead the design, development, training and evaluation of advanced AI models.

  • Develop models capable of learning underlying patterns in energy demand and system behaviour, with the potential to generalise across different applications and environments.

  • Advance intelligent decision-making capabilities that move beyond prediction towards sophisticated reasoning, control and optimisation.

  • Evaluate new architectures and modelling approaches against existing methods, with the ambition to achieve state-of-the-art performance in strategically important areas.

  • Ensure models are technically robust, scalable and capable of being integrated into real-world production environments.

Drive AI research that turns into meaningful products

  • Work closely with engineering, product and commercial teams to ensure Kraken’s technological research addresses core client needs, with the potential to translate into products that deliver measurable value for Kraken and its clients.

  • Help establish the infrastructure, tooling and development practices required to build, evaluate, deploy and continuously improve sophisticated AI systems.

  • Define clear measures of model performance and commercial success, ensuring technical development remains connected to meaningful outcomes.

  • Apply advanced AI models to realtime multi-modal agentic workflows in demanding production environments

  • Build reusable AI capabilities that can support multiple products and business opportunities rather than isolated, one-off solutions.

Influence Kraken's broader AI direction

  • Act as a senior technical authority, helping shape strategic decisions around AI technologies, architectures and investment priorities.

  • Provide technical mentorship and guidance to AI, machine learning and engineering teams across Kraken.

  • Establish high standards for experimentation, model evaluation and responsible deployment.

  • Stay at the forefront literature, developments inAI research, identifying emerging capabilities that could transform software products that underpin the energy industry.

  • Support technical assessments of potential AI partnerships and acquisitions, helping inform build, buy and partner decisions.

🧠 What you’ll bring to the party

We're looking for an exceptional technical leader who has demonstrated the ability to develop advanced AI technology and turn it into real-world impact.

We're more interested in what you've built, the problems you've solved and the technical depth you bring than a particular job title.


Essential experience

  • Deep expertise in modern machine learning and deep learning, with a strong understanding of foundation models, model architectures, and data pipelines.

  • A proven track record of designing, developing or leading the creation of advanced AI models that have delivered measurable technical or commercial outcomes.

  • Strong technical knowledge of several areas such as transformer architectures, foundation-model training and adaptation, representation learning, time-series modelling, reinforcement learning and related machine learning techniques.

  • Experience working with large, complex datasets and developing models capable of identifying meaningful patterns, generalising across problems and operating at scale.

  • A strong understanding of the end-to-end model development lifecycle, including data preparation, training, evaluation, experimentation, inference and production deployment.

  • Experience building, leading or technically guiding high-performing teams of machine learning engineers, research engineers or applied AI specialists.

  • The ability to translate ambitious technical ideas into clear strategies, practical roadmaps and systems that create meaningful business value.

  • Strong technical judgement, including the ability to evaluate emerging approaches, challenge assumptions and make pragmatic decisions about where to invest.

  • The ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and influence senior engineering, product and executive stakeholders.

Technical expertise

You'll bring significant depth in some of the following areas:

  • Foundation models, large language models and transformer-based architectures.

  • Large-scale pre-training, fine-tuning, distillation and model evaluation.

  • Time-series foundation models, representation learning and alternative approaches to structuring and tokenising complex data.

  • Reinforcement learning, decision-making models and learning-based optimisation.

  • Distributed model training and modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX.

  • Scalable data pipelines, training infrastructure, inference systems and production ML engineering.

  • Model evaluation, experimentation and techniques for improving performance, reliability and generalisation.

We don't expect you to be an expert in every area. What matters most is deep technical expertise, the ability to recognise promising approaches and the judgement to build the right capabilities around you.

⭐️ Bonus Points

  • PhD Machine Learning, neuroscience, Computer Science, Physics or a related discipline.

  • Experience developing foundation models or advanced AI systems using large-scale data.

  • Nice to have: experience with energy systems, electricity markets, demand forecasting, grid flexibility or other complex physical systems.

  • Experience applying AI to scientific, industrial or real-world decision-making problems.

  • Experience developing novel model architectures or achieving state-of-the-art results in a commercially relevant domain.

  • Experience establishing a new technical team, capability or product area from an early stage.

title: Head of backend
descriptionHtml:
About SchemeServe

SchemeServe is insurance software like no other.

Hosted in the cloud for MGAs, brokers and insurers, the SchemeServe platform boasts unique flexibility, unstoppable innovation and truly Obsessive Support.

Started in 2000 by our CEO, Adam, SchemeServe has grown from strength to strength, never having taken outside investment. We're proud of how far we've come and how loyal we've stayed to our Core Values.

We're fully remote (we were doing it before it was fashionable!), although we get together twice a year for Team Retreats.

We prize self-development and encourage everyone to keep learning and challenging themselves. Free books? Mentoring? Professional development? You got it.

We also offer flexible working, paid charity days, a fantastic, relaxed and open company culture and free biscuits through the post.

We genuinely believe this is the best place you could ever work.

If you're excited, good! So are we.

Come and join the Insurtech revolution!

Principal Backend Engineer

UK Remote

We're looking for an exceptional Principal Backend Engineer to help make backend engineering across SchemeServe better.

You'll be one of the most technically experienced engineers in the organisation and the CTO's primary technical partner for backend engineering, helping shape our architecture, engineering principles and technical direction.

But this isn't primarily a feature delivery role and your job isn't to personally build everything you help design.

Your real job is to make our engineering organisation better at building great software.

You'll work alongside engineers and teams, helping solve difficult problems, challenging their thinking and developing their technical skills and judgement.

What We Mean By Principal



This is a deeply technical role.

You'll need the depth to understand complex backend systems, architecture, security, performance, resilience and maintainability; review designs and implementations; spot risks; and challenge experienced engineers.

But technical knowledge alone isn't enough.

We want someone who understands there isn't always one "correct" way to build software.

Patterns, standards and best practices are useful tools. They aren't commandments.

We care about finding the most appropriate solution to the problem in front of us.

That means understanding the problem, business, existing platform, risks and likely future – and making pragmatic decisions based on the trade-offs.

Sometimes the right answer will be a new service or technology.

Sometimes it'll be improving what we already have.

Sometimes the boring solution really is the best solution.

We're quite comfortable with that.

How You'll Lead



Success in this role comes through influence rather than authority.

We don't want every difficult technical decision to end with:

"We'd better ask the Principal Engineer."

If an engineer proposes an approach you disagree with, we don't just want you to replace it with your own.

Understand their thinking. Ask questions. Challenge assumptions. Explore the trade-offs. Share your experience.

And be prepared to change your own mind too.

The goal is to leave that engineer better equipped to solve the next problem, not just holding the answer to this one.

Your technical impact should multiply through the people around you.

You'll remain close enough to the code to understand what's actually happening and occasionally roll up your sleeves to prototype, investigate a difficult problem or unblock a team.

But if after a year you've personally written loads of brilliant software while everyone around you is working exactly as they were before, we haven't succeeded.

The Technical Challenge



Our platform has been evolving for more than 25 years.

At its heart is a mature C# .NET Framework 4.7 monolith, alongside an expanding ecosystem of modern C# .NET 10 and TypeScript services.

Our backend estate includes:


  • .NET Framework and modern C#/.NET.
  • TypeScript services.
  • Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Redis.
  • Azure cloud infrastructure.
  • Cloudflare platform services.
  • API-first architecture.
  • Git-based development workflows.


We're continuing to modernise, but we're not interested in modernisation for modernisation's sake.

We aren't trying to win an award for having the most fashionable architecture diagram.

We want a secure, reliable and maintainable platform that can support SchemeServe for many years to come – and we want you to help us decide what should evolve and, just as importantly, what doesn't need changing.

What You'll Do



You'll work closely with our CTO and engineering teams to:


  • Shape our backend engineering strategy, architecture and technical direction.
  • Help engineers make better technical and architectural decisions.
  • Develop sensible engineering principles and guardrails without replacing good judgement with rules.
  • Guide the continued evolution of our monolith and modern service-based platform.
  • Coach and mentor engineers, developing their technical skills and judgement.
  • Review significant designs and architectural decisions and challenge unnecessary complexity.
  • Champion security, quality, testing, observability, resilience and performance.
  • Identify technical risks and help teams navigate them.
  • Evaluate technologies and patterns based on their value to SchemeServe rather than their popularity elsewhere.
  • Balance long-term engineering quality with short-term business needs.
  • Occasionally contribute directly to implementation when that's genuinely the best way to help.
  • Be a generally awesome person.


What We're Looking For



You'll need:


  • Deep expertise in modern backend engineering and strong commercial C#/.NET experience.
  • Strong knowledge of software architecture, distributed systems and API design.
  • Experience with mature legacy applications and modern service-oriented architectures.
  • Strong cloud architecture experience, ideally Azure.
  • Excellent understanding of databases, security, testing, maintainability and modern software delivery.
  • Experience shaping engineering principles and practices across teams.
  • A track record of making engineers around you better through mentoring, coaching and technical leadership.
  • The ability to challenge experienced engineers constructively without becoming a gatekeeper.
  • Strong opinions, loosely held – the confidence to challenge and the humility to change your mind.
  • Excellent communication and the ability to influence without relying on authority.
  • Excellent technical judgement, balancing quality, complexity, risk, cost and business value.


Most importantly, we're looking for someone who asks:

"What's the right solution for us?"

rather than:

"What's the way everyone else is doing it?"

Nice To Have


  • Experience modernising large monolithic applications.
  • Commercial TypeScript backend experience.
  • Cloudflare or edge technology experience.
  • SaaS platforms at scale.
  • Financial services, insurance or another regulated industry.
  • Observability, platform engineering or SRE experience.
  • AI-assisted development and engineering productivity tooling.


You don't need to tick every box.

If you've got the technical depth, judgement and ability to make engineers around you better, we'd rather have a conversation than lose a great candidate because you haven't used one particular technology.

What Success Looks Like



Within your first year:


  • Engineers are making stronger technical and architectural decisions with greater confidence.
  • Our engineering principles are understood rather than blindly followed.
  • Technical discussions are constructive, pragmatic and result in clear decisions.
  • Security, reliability, maintainability and performance concerns are identified earlier.
  • We've made sensible progress modernising our platform without adding complexity for complexity's sake.
  • You've made a lasting positive impact on both our software and the people who build it.


Ultimately, we don't want SchemeServe to become dependent on you for every difficult technical decision.

We want SchemeServe to become better at making those decisions because you're here.

Why Join SchemeServe?

  • Twice-yearly company retreats.
  • Flexible working.
  • Dedicated professional development support.
  • Paid charity days.

title: Head of Financial Controller
descriptionHtml:
🌀 The Company

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

 

🎯 The Role

As Head of Financial Controller, you will own the full accounting function across Filigran's entities, including revenue recognition, consolidation, monthly and year-end close, and internal controls. You will act as the finance function's technical backbone building the infrastructure, controls, and processes needed to support a fast-scaling, multi-entity, international organization.

You will report directly to the VP of Finance. The team is small so this role demands both strategic ownership and significant hands-on execution.

💼 Your Responsibilities

General Accounting Operations

  • Own the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of all financial transactions across Filigran entities

  • Continuously improve a scalable monthly/quarterly close process

  • Ensure revenue recognition is correctly applied and documented

Multi-Entity Oversight

  • Lead consolidation across Filigran's growing international entity structure (including new entity set-ups as the company expands)

  • Partner with the VP of Finance on transfer pricing, inter company transactions, and cross-border compliance matters

Controls, Risk & Governance

  • Perform ongoing gap analyses of accounting processes and proactively design and implement internal controls and policies

  • Manage the yearly financial audit end-to-end, acting as the primary point of contact for auditors

  • Own the relationship with the external accounting firm, holding them to a high standard of accuracy and responsiveness

Systems & Scalability

  • Identify opportunities to automate and streamline accounting workflows

  • Build documentation that make the accounting function auditable and transferable

title: Head of Product Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering leadership myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means an engineering leader who can still ship. Someone who owns the engineering end-to-end — the technical decisions, the pace, and the people who will lead the teams —and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.


What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own hiring and the team shape. Take over engineering hiring and build a process that runs without my oversight. Decide how the team is organised as it grows, and which lead roles we hire or grow into first. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.


What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is running engineering: the organisation and the technical direction. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.

You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

  • Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

  • Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

  • Organisation and leadership. Team structure, performance reviews, the hiring plan, and the managers and tech leads who will run the teams.

  • AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: You have shown you can be one of the top performers in the team and coached others to perform better. The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've hired and grown the first engineering /tech leads, and the structure will hold through the next doubling.


How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

  • Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.

    To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

  • Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

  • AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.

  • Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.

  • We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

This role is for you if:

  • You've led an engineering org and made it ship faster. You've hired great senior engineers and helped them grow into leaders before, run the hard conversations, and know what breaks as a team grows from 10 to 20 in the AI era — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.

  • You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.

  • You have an exceptional IC track record before becoming a manager. You were a senior/principal engineer before you started managing — you didn't skip into management early because coding wasn't working out.

  • You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.

  • You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations about performance.

  • You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.

  • You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."

  • You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.

  • You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.


What we're looking for

Required

  • 10+ years as a software engineer, including 6+ years leading engineering teams and 2+ years managing managers or tech leads

  • You've grown an engineering team to 15+ at a VC-funded startup and hired most of it yourself. You've been through the messy middle, not just read about it

  • You've built what a growing team needs from scratch — hiring process, levels, performance reviews, salary bands — and kept it lightweight

  • You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data

  • Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't

  • You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt

  • You're an engineer at heart. You were senior or principal before you managed, and you can still hold your own in a design review, a debugging session, or building a feature

  • You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook

  • Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK

Nice to have

  • You've grown an engineering org past 20 in the AI era

  • You've taken an engineering team through an ISO 27001 or SOC 2 audit, so you know our customers' side of the product

  • You've led engineering for a B2B SaaS product moving from SMB into mid-market

Interview process

We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process:

  • 30 min — Intro call with our talent team

  • 45 min — Interview with Grigory

  • 60 min — Technical interview

  • 1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI

  • 2 hr — Leadership session with the founders

Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why.


What Secfix gives you

  • Remote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather

  • Salary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk)

  • Equity: Generous package — we're all owners here

  • Development budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better

  • Workspace: Remote workspace support + co-working access

  • Holidays: 26 days + local public holidays

  • Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage

  • Annual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish Islands

  • Tech: MacBook, monitors, headphones — the latest

title: Health Data Protection and Data Licensing Consultant
descriptionHtml:
About Intelance

Intelance is an independent technology, AI and cyber assurance firm based in the UK. We help organisations check, govern and improve their technology through enterprise architecture, AI governance, cyber assurance and data governance work. We are building a small panel of senior associates to deliver technology and AI due diligence on company sales and investments.

The role

You will check whether a company has the legal right to use the health data its business depends on, as part of technology due diligence for clients who are selling, buying or investing in data and AI companies. Buyers in life sciences want to know that client data is handled lawfully, deleted when it should be, and not used for anything the contracts do not allow.

You report to an Intelance engagement partner and work with our technology due diligence lead, who brings your findings into the final report.

What you will do

  • Confirm who is the controller and who is the processor for each type of data, and check the data processing agreements in place.

  • Review client contracts to see whether client data may be used to improve AI workflows, test suites or models.

  • Check how data is deleted when contracts end, and whether that is possible where data has shaped models or tests.

  • Review licences for real world data from third party providers, and what happens to them if the company changes owner.

  • Check data transfers outside the UK, including any use of outside AI providers.

  • Check HIPAA readiness where US health data is involved.

  • Rate each finding by how it could affect the deal, and write clear, practical fixes.

What you will bring

  • At least five years advising on data protection in health, pharmaceutical or life sciences settings.

  • Strong working knowledge of UK GDPR, EU GDPR and international data transfers. HIPAA knowledge is a strong plus.

  • Experience reviewing data processing agreements and data licences.

  • A recognised qualification such as CIPP/E or the BCS Practitioner Certificate, or legal practice in data protection.

  • Clear, plain writing that founders, buyers and lawyers can follow.

  • Experience of AI and data rights, or of due diligence work, is a strong plus.

How the work is set up

  • Remote within the UK, with occasional meetings in London.

  • Around 3 to 5 days between late November 2026 and the end of January 2027, with further engagements as the practice grows.

  • Freelance, or through your own limited company, at £450 to £600 a day depending on experience. Reasonable travel costs for client meetings are covered.

  • A panel agreement, NDA and statement of work are signed before any client details are shared.

  • You work from an Intelance mailbox and use our evidence log and report templates, so every report meets the same standard.

How to apply

Send your CV and answer the short screening questions. They take about two minutes. We aim to reply to every shortlisted candidate within five working days.

This role is within The Goat Agency, a leading brand within WPP Media, where you will be instrumental in helping global brands harness the power of social and creator-led content to deliver measurable impact. Recognised as a global leader in the space, we deliver award-winning campaigns in more than 70 countries. This role is instrumental in supporting the execution of regional strategy, driving key projects, and ensuring local market leads are equipped for success. While an individual contributor role, it requires a high degree of autonomy in project management and the ability to influence cross-functional teams.

Key Responsibilities:

  1. Strategic Support & Operational Enablement:
  • Act as the primary support to Goat EMEA leadership in translating regional objectives into actionable plans and ensuring their successful execution.

  1. Relationship & Stakeholder Coordination:

  • Support Goat EMEA leadership in fostering a cohesive and high-performance culture by coordinating internal communications and sharing best practices across European teams.

Skills and Competencies:

  • Senior Project & Operational Management Experience: Proven track record (typically 5+ years) in a senior project management, operational support, or strategic coordination role within a digital marketing, advertising, or influencer marketing agency, with significant exposure to European markets.
  • Collaborative Leadership: Demonstrated ability to effectively partner with senior leadership as a trusted strategic and operational enabler, supporting strategic initiatives and driving execution through influence and collaboration rather than direct authority.
  • Exceptional Organizational & Problem-Solving Skills: Highly organized with meticulous attention to detail, capable of managing multiple complex projects concurrently and adept at identifying, analysing, and solving operational challenges.
  • Strong Communication & Presentation Abilities: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex information clearly, prepare compelling presentations, and effectively engage with diverse stakeholders.
  • Strategic Acumen: Ability to understand high-level strategic objectives and translate them into actionable plans, contributing insightful perspectives to regional discussions.
  • Market & Ecosystem Knowledge: Familiarity with the European media, marketing, and creator economy landscape, and an understanding of agency operations and dynamics within the WPP network.
  • Proactive & Self-Directed: A highly motivated self-starter who can work autonomously, take initiative, and consistently deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

Our passion for shaping the next era of media is powered by our commitment to Be Extraordinary, investing in our employees to inspire transformational creativity. We also Lead Optimistically, firmly believing in and Championing Growth and Development for every individual. title: Infrastructure Software Engineering – Platform & Build
descriptionHtml:
About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

The Role

As an Infrastructure Platform Engineer you will be a core part of our technical team working alongside the hardware, software and research teams to solve cutting-edge problems in AI hardware, ranging from verification to simulation, alongside the best of the best (DeepMind, Apple, Meta…).

About the Software organisation at Fractile

Infrastructure sits within the Software organisation at Fractile, which is responsible for developing a full software stack for our groundbreaking AI inference systems. That's everything from ML compilers, device drivers and systems firmware, application level runtime and ecosystem integrations, ML and compute libraries, great developer tooling and a full portfolio of simulators, through to datacenter scale workload deployment solutions. At Fractile, we know that a fantastic software stack is a critical and central part of any AI inference solution and it sits at the heart of everything we're doing.

About the team and role

The Infrastructure team is responsible for the core platform and systems at Fractile. We build, scale, and optimize the mission-critical systems that power our entire engineering org, including our multi-language Bazel monorepo and CI pipelines. From hardware design and verification to kernel development and ML compilers, we enable all Fractile engineers to ship fast and reliably.

The team brings both deep build system expertise and an SRE mindset: reliability, build performance, debugging CI failures systematically, and giving the engineering organisation clear visibility into how our infrastructure is performing.

As an Infrastructure Platform Engineer, you will:

  • Own the CI infrastructure end-to-end: create, maintain and debug reproducible multi-language CI pipelines, and optimize CI performance across large compute clusters.

  • Build and maintain infrastructure observability, alerting, runbooks, and incident response workflows for Fractile's infrastructure.

title: Innovative Project Planner (Data Centres / Buildings / High-tech / Infrastructure) - UK (Hybrid)
descriptionHtml:
Are you a bit tired of the standard, old-fashioned way of doing things in the construction industry? Do you get deep satisfaction from making things run more efficiently using a good dose of common sense and maybe a bit of technology? Have you always cared about the importance of proper planning and the connection between the schedule and the real, day-to-day delivery of the job? Have you ever wanted to work a bit more flexibly but still be hands-on in construction and improving the industry? Sounds like a dream. Well, it isn’t. It’s quite real! Read on. ____________________________________________________________ We are Laminar Projects! If you’ve already heard about us, you’re probably reading this because you’re tired of the typical, chaotic ways of doing things in construction. But in case you haven’t, we’re a high-end project management consultancy and tech developer with a focus on upgrading the way construction projects are delivered. Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Check out our short film about it.) We bring transparency and control to projects through a pragmatic mix of the latest tech, our own processes, and a big dose of common sense. We then take our deep understanding of these projects and we invest heavily into developing the digital solutions that anyone can use to deliver their projects better. (Check out Shape, our construction management tech, to see what we’re doing.) The core of all this is our true secret sauce: our people. We only recruit the very best, both in capability and personality. We’re deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that’s optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People who join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined. (Read more about our vision and missions.) This approach has allowed us to grow from just two people in 2017 to over 220 today. We have a stable, repeat client base across infrastructure and complex building projects in the UK and internationally, and we’re still growing fast. Joining us isn’t just some “job”. It’s a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life. There are many diverse and interesting challenges available. It’s up to you to guide yourself into whichever areas you’re most interested – we’ll enable it. (Get to know us better by watching a few more of our videos.) Core values for a good life A life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships and challenging yourself to create a positive impact, so our values reflect the four levels of relationships that each of us has: - Grow yourself – your relationship with yourself - Care about people – your relationship with others around you - Execute to greatness – your relationship with your team - Build civilisation – your relationship with humanity and the world We enshrined our values in our vision: We exist so that everyone in our team can flourish in a high-impact community that: - Connects us with meaningful relationships - Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans - Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures By first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world. And enable the achievement of our vision through our two missions: - To fully digitalise the construction of human civilisation - To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society ____________________________________________________________ The Role Purpose of the role You’ll be enhancing the delivery of the most complex and interesting projects in the world through the power of project planning to the very highest standards. You’ll devise strategies and tactics to improve the way the project is delivered. You’ll translate this knowledge into a logic-linked plan and analyse it using planning software. Then you’ll use the plan to help the teams understand what to prioritise. Your team This role is part of our Project Management Consultancy team which focuses on: - Understanding what the real problems of projects are - Implementing the best solutions to those problems - Developing scalable best practices, tools and technology More specifically, you’ll be part of our Project Planning Team, who are industry leaders in the planning of complex construction projects. Your initial leader will be one of our planning discipline directors. Your top three objectives 1. To make construction projects deliver to near perfection 2. To create scalable and repeatable solutions to common problems 3. To develop yourself and everyone around you Your top five responsibilities 1. Own the plan: Own the project plan for one or more projects and ensure that the project is working to it effectively. Ensure delays are mitigated and managed commercially 2. Own the outcome: You're responsible for putting in your best effort to ensure the project team’s understanding and focus on the plan – no matter how stubborn they are 3. Report and inform: Provide simple, actionable reports to stakeholders at all levels that help them deliver their part of the project more efficiently and effectively 4. Make scalable solutions: Develop scalable and repeatable best practices and tools in collaboration with the team so that long-term impact is achieved 5. Develop everyone: Maximise the development of your team personally and professionally and educate our clients to improve as well You must have: - A construction engineering background: You have at least 2+ years of experience on construction projects, experience in project planning both software and principles, as well as decent Excel skills, and a strong interest in data - Communication skills: You’re proficient in written and verbal English and have the charisma and influence to get construction people to do new things and take the best approach - Leadership capabilities: You lead yourself proactively and lead others by asking the right questions and challenging them - Impact: You have a track record of making projects and organisations better beyond just doing the basics – implementing scalable, repeatable solutions that had a significant positive impact Laminar isn’t the place for you if any of the following is true: - You want an easy, chilled-out role without much challenge - You like to be the smartest person in the room - You don’t like continuously receiving honest candid feedback - You prefer to do your own thing rather than work with a team ____________________________________________________________ Frequently Asked Questions What kinds of projects would I be working on? It’s common for people to be exposed to several projects in their first year with us. You’ll work on some of the most complex and interesting environments in the world. We’ve delivered over 100 data centres internationally, many of them fast-tracked and multi-package. Our teams have supported flagship infrastructure programmes like HS2 through integrated planning and digital delivery, contributed to over $30bn in power generation and transmission projects, and played a key role in the development of high-containment labs and R&D campuses for some of the world’s most advanced industrial and life sciences clients. You might find yourself working in sectors such as data centres, infrastructure (including defense, rail, and highways), high tech (such as advanced manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and semiconductors), or complex building projects. These aren’t hands-off assignments. They’re dynamic, hands-on environments designed for people who want to be challenged. We bring back the lessons from every project to help our team grow and deliver the highest levels of value. (Check out our case stories.) Who are our clients? Major owners/operators and main contractors with project values between £1m and £1bn+ globally. Where would I be working? One week you might be working from home. The next, you might travel to the site to meet the construction teams and help organise them. Maybe you’ll pop into our London office for a workshop or a beer. Maybe you’ll fly out to exotic (and sometimes not!) locations in Europe or the Middle East to visit clients. It really depends on what you want to get involved in and what fits with your life. How does what I do connect with the long-term impact on the construction industry? You’re tasked with understanding and solving common problems. We don’t want to reinvent the wheel every time, so you’ll be responsible for documenting new solutions and evolving ones we’ve developed. This goes into our knowledge repository, which we’re going to open source to the industry. The knowledge you capture will be used by us to build new products. You’ll constantly test those products in the field, so we can rapidly iterate and improve them for anyone in the industry to use. ____________________________________________________________ Benefits The standard stuff: - Health Insurance Scheme. Comprehensive private health coverage – for you and your family. Because your well-being is our priority - Pension Scheme. A competitive plan to help you plan for the long term – plus salary sacrifice options available to maximise your savings - Bonus Scheme. As a permanent member of the team, you’ll share in our success. Our annual bonus is designed to reward both the now and the future – with a flexible mix of cash and high-growth equity that you choose. Bonuses are discretionary and based on performance - Professional body membership. One fee covered per year – so you can stay connected to your field and develop your craft - Cycle to Work Scheme. A tax-efficient way to get wheels – and do your bit for the environment The life-changing stuff: - In-house coaching. Regular 1:1 coaching sessions, fully confidential, to help you navigate challenges, build self-awareness, and grow intentionally – professionally and as a human being - Equity upside. As we grow, you grow. Our generous equity scheme is especially powerful for those who stay with us on our journey. You help us build the future – and own a piece of it - Flexible working. Work where it makes sense – most of our team works from home, visiting sites or clients regularly. We care about outcomes, not clock-ins - Relentless development. Our goal is for every year here to be worth five years of development anywhere else. You’ll get a coach, a mentor, honest feedback, and a culture that challenges you to keep levelling up ____________________________________________________________ Important! Applying properly We get thousands of applications so please write us a letter as part of your application explaining: - Why you want to join us - What you’ll bring to the team We aren't a giant, faceless corporation; we really care about the people who want to join our team, so your letter will be read carefully. After that, we’ll reach out to you to schedule a casual conversation to help you get to know us a bit better and tell us a bit about yourself. A couple of technical and personal assessments follow to understand your capability based on our own development matrix. This is to ensure that when you join, you’re starting at the right level of responsibility.

title: Insurance Product Manager / Underwriter (P&C)
descriptionHtml:
Most insurance product roles ask you to perfect one product in one market. This one asks you to build Europe’s SME insurance products: decide what we cover and who we insure, negotiate it with our carriers and get it live, market after market.

Deep in the wording. Fast in the build.

About Insify

Insurance for entrepreneurs is still built the old way: one market at a time, wordings nobody reads, and cover that leaves out the very businesses that need it most.

We're doing it differently.

Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by €43M in total funding from world-class investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years, we've expanded from the Netherlands into France, Germany and Ireland, and we're just getting started. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

We aren't just building a company; we're leading a revolution. Our culture is intense, high-stakes, and mission-driven. We hire smart, ambitious "owners" who possess a relentless drive to win. This is an environment for those who thrive on challenges, value intellectual honesty, and share our mindset of becoming a global category leader.

Our founding team consists of seasoned entrepreneurs who have previously built iconic businesses like HelloFresh, Bloomon, and SumUp. We bring that same bias for speed, scale, and high standards to one of the most structurally broken experiences in financial services. Together, we combine that deep fintech and e-commerce expertise with cutting-edge AI to stay ahead of the curve.


What you’ll own in your first year

You won’t inherit a finished product shelf. You’ll build the engine that fills it.

  1. Build the product engine. Turn how we benchmark a market into a system: compare cover, limits and exclusions across local players, our Dutch home product and our other markets, so every new product starts from facts, not gut feeling.
  2. Make the call on cover. Decide what we cover, what we don’t and who we insure, and turn it into a proposal. The tools do the comparison; the judgment is yours.
  3. Get it signed. Take the proposal to our risk carriers and negotiate it. You know what to push on, what to let go and which clause will set off six red flags.
  4. Get it live. Adapt our wordings to each new market, run the legal review and launch. Less writing from scratch, more making one strong product fit the next market. Then track loss ratios, competition and customer feedback, and sharpen it.
  5. Build what doesn’t exist yet. In the markets where we double down, own custom products from the insurance side, including cover for the trades and businesses others decline.

Who you are

You’re an insurance expert first and a builder second, but a real one.

  • You have 5+ years hands-on in commercial P&C (Property & Casualty) at an insurer, MGA, (re)insurer or specialist broker, across underwriting, product and wordings, ideally for SMEs.
  • You know what is covered, what isn’t and what should be. Hand you a wording from a market you’ve never worked in and you’ll spot the gaps within minutes.
  • You’ve worked across more than one line, product or market, and you can apply what you know to a market you’ve never seen.
  • You’ve sat at the table with insurers or capacity providers and know where the red lines are.
  • You’d rather fix insurance than complain about it. Maybe you already tried: at an insurtech, an MGA, your own startup, or on the carrier side building products with insurtechs.
  • You think like the customer: plain questions, fair cover, and no excluding everything just to be safe.
  • You’re at home in Excel and data, and curious about what automation and LLMs can take off your plate. You don’t need to code; our product and tech teams build the digital journey with you.
  • You work fluently in English; German, French or Dutch is a big plus.

    • What we offer
  • Real ownership. You decide what we cover and work directly with the MT, close to where decisions get made.
  • Range. More products and markets in a year than most people see in a decade at an incumbent.
  • A share in what we build. Equity, so you share in the value you build.
  • A team that cares. We live by four values: Grit, Care, Impact and Entrepreneurship.
  • Growth. Room to grow into leading our insurance product work as we add markets, plus an in-house coaching and leadership program.
  • The package. Competitive salary package + 6% pension, holidays, well-being budget and rich social events (ski trip, summer and winter party).
  • The basics, done well. Office in central Amsterdam, laptop, hybrid working. Relocation support.
